title: Prompt-injection defence for fetched research content, with a both-states test
question_or_target: What filter reliably neutralises instruction-shaped text in fetched pages, tool results and PDFs before it reaches a reasoning context - structural quarantine, provenance tagging, instruction-stripping, or capability withdrawal during synthesis - and what is its measured catch rate against a corpus of 30 real and synthetic injection payloads?
tests_required: both-states control: include 10 benign documents that legitimately QUOTE instruction-like text (a document about prompt injection necessarily contains injection strings) and require the filter not to mangle them - the use-versus-mention failure this estate has hit repeatedly
note: Frozen excerpt of the catalog unit used as a local estate source. Not a live web fetch.
